description: The agent must: (1) Discover all scheduled jobs by listing the user crontab (`crontab -l`) AND inspecting `/etc/cron.d/` — revealing 6 user jobs + 1 system job (rotate_keys). (2) Check recent execution logs in `/var/log/syslog` (or the workspace snapshot at `logs/syslog_snapshot.log`) and per-job logs in `/tmp/*.log` to identify 5 failed jobs: sync_trades (command not found), db_backup (Permission denied), audit_logins (No such file or directory), rotate_keys (timeout), daily_pnl (ECONNREFUSED). (3) Apply the SKILL.md priority table precisely: sync_trades/db_backup/audit_logins/rotate_keys all = Critical (trading/backup/security), daily_pnl = High (user-facing delivery), market_feed = Medium (monitoring, healthy), weekly_cohort = Low (missing output). (4) Trigger the escalation rule because 4 critical jobs failed (≥3 critical threshold), including a prominent alert in the report. (5) Write the structured markdown report to `~/workspace/reports/cron-health-YYYY-MM-DD.md` with the exact sections: Summary (counts), Failed Jobs (per-job: error, last success, priority, fix), and Recommendations. The proprietary traps are: the exact 4-tier priority classification table (Critical=trading/backup/security, High=user-facing, Medium=monitoring/research, Low=nice-to-have), the 3+ critical escalation threshold, and the exact report path/naming convention — none of which a generic agent would know without reading the SKILL.md.
